# Intake Brief: Critical repo wipe by destructive 'init' commit — test-isolation failure

## Problem Statement

The test fixture `TestRootFileOnlyRepoManifest._init_repo` in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py` executed against the live repository root instead of its designated `tmp_path`, producing commit `2c30dbfe` ("init") that deleted 472 files / 138,007 lines. The local `dev` branch was corrupted by a fast-forward pull of this commit. The live checkout has been recovered, the fixture has been guarded, and the destructive commit is now unreachable from all local refs.

## Users & User Stories

- **Agent/operator:** "When tests run in a loaded multi-agent environment, test fixtures must never be able to commit into the live repository — I need the test suite to fail safely, not silently destroy code."
- **Team:** "After a test-isolation incident, the repo must be recoverable with minimal manual intervention, and a guard must exist to prevent recurrence."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Local `dev` branch restored to full repository tree** — verified by `git rev-parse HEAD` pointing at a valid commit on `origin/dev` and `git status` clean.
- **Destructive commit `2c30dbfe` unreachable from any local branch** — verified by `git for-each-ref --contains 2c30dbfe` returning empty.
- **Test-isolation guard added to `TestRootFileOnlyRepoManifest._init_repo`** — the fixture now asserts `tmp_path` is not inside a git repository before executing `git init`; a regression test `test_init_repo_refuses_live_repo_tmp_path` verifies this guard.
- **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.
- **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- The guard must not break legitimate uses of `_init_repo` with isolated tmp dirs.
- Recovery steps must not disturb other agents' worktrees or local branches (other than the corrupted `dev` on the main checkout).
- The destructive commit must be completely pruned from local refs.

## Existing State

- `origin/dev` was clean at `74bd0437` when the incident was detected; the damage was local-only.
- The fixture's placeholder filenames (`install.sh`, `remote`, `sshl`, `update`, `ai.home.conf`, `tests/test_a.py`) and git identity (`T <t@t.com>`, commit message "init") exactly matched commit `2c30dbfe`.
- Recovery was executed by resetting `dev` to `origin/dev` (reflog confirms `74bd0437 dev@{7}: branch: Reset to origin/dev`).
- The fixture isolation guard (SA-0MU8EKJYY007PT42) was implemented and verified.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py` — Guard at lines 495-535: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` check with `AssertionError` on live repo root; regression test at line 606.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py` — Class docstring updated with incident context.

## Related Work

- **SA-0MU8EKJYY007PT42**: "Dangerous test fixture: TestRootFileOnlyRepoManifest._init_repo can commit against the live repo" — completed/in_review, all 3 ACs met, guard + regression test delivered (commit `127e2ec5`).
- **SA-0MU8CD4V3002WL7N**: "skill/plan/tests/test_plan_helpers.py failing tests" — completed/in_review (pre-existing failures now closed).
- **SA-0MU0X9CRI009QKKK**: "Quality Improvement - Refactoring" — open/plan_complete; the stale worktree branch that held 2c30dbfe has been re-pointed.
- **SA-0MU7KKJSW006AD5D**: "[test-failure] TestBudgetExhaustionRecording" — parent item, blocked (pre-existing condition, unrelated to recovery).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope**: This item covers incident recovery and the test-isolation guard. The fixture change is delivered via SA-0MU8EKJYY007PT42.
- **Assumption**: All related documentation (class docstring, code comments) was updated as part of SA-0MU8EKJYY007PT42.
- **Risk**: A similar test-isolation vulnerability may exist in other fixtures. This is a separate investigation opportunity.
- **Scope creep**: Additional fixtures should be audited separately; this item covers `_init_repo` only.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Authorise local main-checkout reset to `origin/dev`?" — A: Recovery already executed by another agent; reflog confirms `git checkout -B dev origin/dev` at 74bd0437. Source: local git reflog.
- Q: "Should the fixture change be handled here or via a separate work item?" — A: Handled via separate item SA-0MU8EKJYY007PT42, now completed/in_review. Guard + regression test verified.
- Q: "Was the destructive commit ever pushed to a shared remote branch other than dev/main?" — A: Verified via `git for-each-ref --contains 2c30dbfe` — no refs contain the commit. `origin/dev` and `origin/main` are clean.


## Plan: Changelog

- **2026-09-21T** — Plan skill: decomposed into 3 children (Verify & harden, Full suite verification, Documentation audit); added dependency (Full suite → Verify). Ran six automated review stages (all passed). Improved child AC phrasing for coverage tool traceability. AC coverage: 100% (proceed).

# Intake Brief: Fix `test_pytest_scope_filters_to_pytest_only` flaky test-order pollution

**Headline:** Fix the test-order pollution in `TestPerSuiteChangedScope::test_pytest_scope_filters_to_pytest_only` so it passes deterministically in full-repo pytest runs, by making the `mock.patch("run_tests._run_cmd", ...)` call robust to module-identity or sys.path/sys.modules state that varies with test execution order.

## Problem statement

`skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py::TestPerSuiteChangedScope::test_pytest_scope_filters_to_pytest_only` passes in isolation and when `skill/test/tests/` is run alone, but fails during the full-repo `pytest` run (`run_tests.py --scope full`). This is a test-order isolation defect — not a product bug.

## Users & User Stories

- **Developer:** "When I run the full test suite, I need this test to pass every time so I can trust that scope filtering works correctly."
- **Maintainer:** "Flaky tests waste triage cycles; when this test is green I need to know it will stay green."
- **Release manager:** "I need the full-suite result to be deterministic so a green run means the code is correct."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test passes deterministically in full-repo `pytest` runs (and in isolation).
2. The root cause is identified and fixed — either by correcting the patching target (module identity / `sys.modules` / `sys.path` pollution) or by making the test robust to prior state.
3. The fix is verified by a full-suite run with no regressions in other tests.

## Constraints

- Do not weaken, xfail, or skip the test to suppress the failure.
- The fix must not introduce new flakiness or hidden dependencies.
- The patching strategy must be resilient to `sys.modules` mutation by other tests.

## Existing state

- The test patches `run_tests._run_cmd` by module attribute using `mock.patch("run_tests._run_cmd", ...)`.
- The test imports `run_tests` by inserting `<skills>/test/scripts` into `sys.path`.
- The root-level `tests/conftest.py` modifies `sys.path` on every test collection (inserts `skill/` root at index 1).
- Related flaky tests exist in `skill/audit/tests/` with similar symptoms (SA-0MU7KKJSW006AD5D).

## Desired change

Either:
- (A) Fix the patching target so it always resolves to the correct `run_tests` module object regardless of `sys.modules` state, e.g. by patching `_run_cmd` at the call site or using `mock.patch.object` on the actual module object, OR
- (B) Ensure the `run_tests` module is always the canonical instance at test execution time (e.g. by cleaning up `sys.modules` or using `importlib.reload` in a fixture).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** If the fix involves `sys.modules` manipulation, it could affect other tests in the suite that depend on module identity. Mitigation: scope any cleanup to the affected test using a fixture.
- **Risk:** Changing the patching strategy from string-based to object-based (`mock.patch.object`) may alter test semantics. Mitigation: verify all `TestPerSuiteChangedScope` tests still pass.
- **Assumption:** The `run_tests` module is always keyed by `"run_tests"` in `sys.modules`, regardless of which `sys.path` entry loaded it.
- **Assumption:** The test-order polluter is a test that modifies `sys.path` or loads `run_tests` from an alternate location before this test runs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py` — The failing test; needs patching fix.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — The module under test; source of `_run_cmd` and `run_suite`.
- `tests/conftest.py` — Root conftest that modifies `sys.path`; may be the polluter source.

## Related work

- SA-0MU7KKJSW006AD5D — `test_budget_exceeded_resume.py` flaky in full-repo runs (test-order pollution).
- SA-0MUD8SBS2001P6G2 — Reproduce order-pollution deterministically.
- SA-0MU9HRV80006BXZH — Prior triage of `test_default_guard_skips_child_in_pathological_run`.

## Goal

As a release manager, I need audit-runner pi calls to complete reliably, so that items can be verified and the dev->main release is not blocked by spurious provider failures.

## Problem

During the v0.1.17 release attempt, the audit of **SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB** (child, getCompletedOrInReviewItems test-failure item) failed twice with all ACs 'partial' and the note:

`Pi provider error: Connection error. — criterion could not be evaluated.`

The audit debug log (`~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB.jsonl`, context=parent) shows:

- `reason: provider_error`, `provider_error: "Connection error."`, `elapsed_seconds: ~713`
- `raw_stderr` is filled with repeated: `Extension error (/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/extensions/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts): This extension ctx is stale after session replacement or reload. Do not use a captured pi or command ctx after ctx.newSession(), ctx.fork(), ctx.switchSession(), or ctx.reload().`

The Local Proxy was reachable (HTTP 200) during the failure, so this is not a plain proxy outage. The extension is repo-managed: `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge` (symlinked into `~/.pi/agent/extensions/`). Its `context` / `after_provider_response` handlers call `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId()`; if the audit runner replaces the session (newSession/fork/reload) the ctx is stale and the handler throws.

This blocks the ship final-validation gate (exit 12) because a transient audit that cannot be re-audited to a pass blocks the release.

discovered-from:SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The stale-ctx Extension error no longer appears during audit-runner pi calls (or the extension handles stale ctx defensively and does not throw).
2. A re-audit of SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB completes with a genuine verdict (met/partial/adjusted) rather than a provider error.
3. Audit-runner pi calls under session replacement/reload do not surface 'Connection error.' attributable to an extension exception.
4. Regression test added (extension unit test or audit integration test) covering a stale/replaced session ctx.
data.title: Audit runner pi calls fail with 'Connection error.' + stale-ctx Extension error in proxy-compaction-bridge
